locator.text: Equation (B.23), p. 150, in the statement of Lemma B.4

evidence: paper: S_{q,\mathrm{r}} \ge .94\,L\Lambda\chi + 2.4, \qquad l_{\mathrm{r}} \le 1, \qquad v_{\mathrm{r}} := p_{1,\mathrm{r}} + \frac{p_{2,\mathrm{r}}^{2}}{p_{1,\mathrm{r}}} > 2 + c.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. All three clauses of (B.23) are stated, as three fields of one structure, with the paper's constants: 47/50 = .94, 12/5 = 2.4, and L h η = 1 - 2hη^2, chi h j σ η = H^2/(H^2+σ^2), matching the paper's L = 1 - 2hη^2 and the regularized cutoff χ = H_*^2/(H_*^2 + σ_*^2) that the paper fixes with χ > .99 where |Z_*| ≤ δ_*. Three deviations, all in the direction of a stronger Lean statement. (i) Sign of the inequality: the paper writes S_{q,r} ≥ .94LΛχ + 2.4, the Lean writes the strict .94·L·Λ·χ + 12/5 < sourceQ, which implies the paper's ≥. (ii) Domain: the paper asserts (B.23) on [X_0, X_i] × [-1,1] with X_0 = 4/Λ, X_i = 110; holdRegion = Icc 0 110 ×ˢ Icc (-1) 1, so the first two clauses are proved on a superset ([0,110] ⊇ [4/Λ,110]), while cone_margin is restricted by the hypothesis 4/Λ ≤ p.1 and so covers exactly [X_0, X_i]. (iii) The paper's constant c in '> 2 + c' is an unnamed fixed positive constant (compare the fixed c_ex > 0 of (B.19), where the paper offers c_ex = .2); the Lean hard-codes 9/4 < coneSize, i.e. the instance c = 1/4, which implies the paper's 'for some fixed c > 0'. Recovery: instantiate c := 1/4 and weaken < to ≤ on the first clause. Noted as a fact about the material, not a difference in the formula: the docstring above exists_reference_bounds (ReferenceBounds.lean:1176) calls it 'Lemma 5.2', the repository's own numbering, not this manuscript's Lemma B.4.
